amends_note: Phase 7.3 (ADR-0018) claimed a scoped decode-CPU win with an explicit NO-bytes-read-win caveat. This campaign supplies and measures the missing seek reader; it does not restate the whole-file axis (still a loss).
phase: Phase 8.3 — seek-based partial I/O: bytes-read court for a seeked view
claim: On a 33,789,340 B (32.22 MiB) deterministic 800-stream PDF whose seekable descriptor is 17,566,832 B, the seeked `view` (which now reads only the 64-byte header, the DIRECTORY, GRAPH, OBSERVATION_INDEX, INTEGRITY, and the one referenced object/channel/model — never the whole file) serves all 18 pre-registered queries byte-exactly and reads a constant 439,679-461,367 B regardless of offset. That is <= 2.6% of the descriptor for every query and, in the late region (>= 50% in, 8/8 queries), 4.7%-21x fewer bytes than gzip's compressed prefix (9,764,864 B at 31 MiB) and ~12-13x fewer than zstd/xz. It also drops peak RSS from ~38 MB to ~3.8 MB and CPU to ~0.00 s. It LOSES on bytes at a=0 versus gzip (327,680 B) and at early queries (<= ~1.7 MiB) versus xz (253,952-368,640 B), because of the constant GRAPH+INDEX+DIRECTORY floor, and would dominate a descriptor smaller than ~9 MB. Whole-file size remains a ~3.01x loss to xz. Single locally generated corpus; no population claim.
command: dev: pdf-make-large 800; tools: qpdf --check + gs; dev: deflate-stats; dev: encode --force pdf-deflate-replay-rans-indexed; baseline: gzip/zstd/xz; baseline: tools/baselines.sh; baseline: tools/seek-court.sh queries.jsonl ...; baseline: jq -rs -f tools/seek-table.jq

tooling.cli_change: src/main.rs cmd_view peeks the 64-byte header and hands the handle to the seek reader; a descriptor with no seek feature keeps the Phase-7 in-memory path

verdict: BYTES-READ WIN (scoped): constant ~0.44-0.46 MB read for mid/late queries versus 2.7-9.8 MB gzip prefixes; loses at a=0 (gzip) and early (xz); whole-file size still a loss

seekable_amendment.phase: 8.4 — seekable/blocked random-access baseline (falsifies the framing that this is a general random-access-I/O win)
seekable_amendment.verdict: NOT a general random-access-I/O win: VOLE reads 2.6-30x MORE than a seekable/blocked format (BGZF ~24 KB; blocked xz 15-180 KB) for the same late query; it loses at offset 0 and early; whole-file is 3.01x xz and 0.46x BGZF. The Phase-8.3 claim stands only versus non-seekable sequential gzip/zstd/xz prefixes.
